- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out immediate peaks.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d), model underestimates mean-reversion zones; adjust downward by 1–3% if recent price is above 30-day average.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–3 day lag correction to reflect sentiment shift.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underestimate final price peaks; add 1–2% buffer if sentiment remains bullish at end of horizon.
